_readme: Prediction layer for the book-log / book-suggest skills. One JSON object per line, keys matching book-cache.json. Estimates are RECOMPUTED BY /book-log (its PROPAGATE phase), never by /book-suggest, which only reads them. Roughly sorted best-first; the order is a convenience, never load-bearing. Access state is NOT in this file: book-cache.json is authoritative for that and nothing here may duplicate it.
_revs: book-revs.json. Nothing in this header line may contain a literal dep id, so that a grep for one returns book lines only.
_est: [low, high] score range, CONDITIONAL on nothing in 'risks' firing. null means 'blocked' names a hard filter the book already fails.
_deps: dep-id -> the rev in 'revs' this estimate was computed under. Valid iff every dep rev still matches. Mandatory minimum on every line (all with the axis: prefix, spelled out here without it so this note is not itself a grep hit): the three taste hard filters opening, occult and detective; the two heaviest graded axes worldbuilding and protagonist; motives; and the author id. A change to any of those cannot miss a book whose estimate never examined it - the Mortal Engines 55 lesson, where the prediction was argued on the opening and lost on the axis it never looked at. axis:access is deliberately NOT a dep: access lives in book-cache.json only.
_leanedOn: the dep(s) actually carrying the number. A change here means re-derive from scratch; a change to a merely-listed dep usually means no move. Both prediction failures so far - Artemis (predicted 80, scored 76) and Mortal Engines 55 - came from leaning on the wrong axis, and this field is what makes that measurable.
_risks: axis ids that could collapse the estimate below its range. Always a subset of deps. Must be stated when the book is proposed.
_invariant: one line here for every book in book-cache.json, and vice versa; no line for a book in books-read.md.

why: The best axis match found in any category screen. Declaring one premise precisely and working out its consequences with total rigour IS Chiang's method, so form one and form two are the product rather than an obligation he might fail - and short idea-driven is the log's safest category, where the character rules are suspended. Higher things to think about is the whole point of the book.

The closest structural analogue to Seeking Allah 91 anywhere in the catalogue: first-person account of leaving Islam, examined belief plus insight into how another group experiences the world - the two things that actually earned that 91, not the memoir form itself, which Anne Frank 40 discredited. Risks are real bleakness and drift toward argument.

The Three Laws are a precisely declared rule system and every story is a consequence derived from them - the strict-rules interest in its purest form, and an idea that can be stated in a sentence. Survives the sharpened rule on its own merits; trimmed only because flat characters and dated prose are no longer offset by a category bonus.

Linked stories carrying declared consequences across a whole arc, and the idea is nameable: colonisation written as elegy rather than adventure. The arc is what earns - each story pays for the one before it, which is the structure face of the heaviest axis, priced by the Tolkien gradient from Silmarillion 80 down to Unfinished Tales 69. Short form removes penalties rather than adding points, so the range rests on the ideas and the arc and not on the length. Bleakness is a mild pushback: the elegiac register is sustained, and 1984 60 is the only book in the log grim enough to have cost real points.
Contemporary, contested, first-person Uyghur testimony - the Qureshi 91 axis rather than the historical-canon form that failed. Bleakness is genuine here and is a mild pushback only.

t: Cekam, az si pro me v noci prijdou
why: A poet's account of getting his family out of Xinjiang ahead of arrest. The memoir form earns nothing by itself - Anne Frank 40 is the same form and failed outright - so this rests on the two things that did earn: examining what is actually true, and insight into how another group experiences the world, the axis behind Seeking Allah 91 and Son of Hamas 75. The surveillance state is documented at the level of one family's decisions, with more interiority than the reportage form usually carries. Bleakness is the standing risk, though 1984 60 is the only book grim enough to have cost real points.

Society as subject with the premise followed through rigorously. Bleak, but the Animal Farm 78 model of bleak-with-ideas rather than immersion in misery, and the child leads are suspended by the short-idea-driven rule.

Short allegory in the Little Prince 82 shape, but the resemblance is formal and the ideas are not. Name the idea and it comes out as 'pursue mastery for its own sake', delivered in an earnest new-age register - thin next to what actually earned the Little Prince its 82. Re-derived 2026-08-26: this was floated on the category rather than on its content, which the sharpened rule no longer allows.

A Syrian monk held by IS - faith carried inside a narrative, which is the stated preference exactly. Risk is the balance tipping from story to devotional reflection, which is the no-theology-as-subject line. Field fix 2026-08-26: axis:faith appeared in both leanedOn and risks, which makes both fields useless; it is kept as the axis carrying the number and the range already expresses the uncertainty. No number changed.

Vonnegut's early slick-magazine work, written to sell to Collier's rather than to argue anything - the voice is there, the ideas are not, and this is explicitly not the canonical Vonnegut. A cheap way to test the author, not a book with a case of its own. Re-derived 2026-08-26.

t: Pribehy vaseho zivota (Stories of Your Life and Others)
why: Downgraded 18 points 2026-08-26: the occult risk this estimate had merely LISTED was researched and it fires. Dvaasedmdesat pismen takes its golem-animation straight from real Kabbalistic and Hermetic name-magic and stages the inscribing as the story's working mechanism, so both tests fail at once - the source is actual occultism rather than an invented system, and the rite is enacted on the page rather than referred to. Occult is the most severe objection in the log and the three books that fail it sit at 51, 53 and 57. What holds this well above them is that the breach is one story of eight and is skippable, not the medium of the whole book: the rest is one premise per story followed to its end, every idea nameable in a phrase, which is the Project Hail Mary 92 axis at story length. A second, smaller deduction on top - Peklo je nepritomnost boha is literal theodicy, faith as the subject rather than a thread inside a story, which the profile excludes separately. The range assumes he reads around both; if he does not, this belongs in the 50s with the other occult failures.

Genuine philosophical weight - the Ridiculous Man's dream is an idea, not a mood - so it survives the sharpened rule. Risks are the 19th-century Russian register and openings that circle before they land: legible, but not immediately gripping, which is the axis the log is most sensitive to.

Immediately legible Edwardian comic stories, and humour is not the objection (cf. Adams 83). But the stories trade on wit and a last-line reversal and leave nothing behind, which is the axis the log is most consistent about - 'wants higher things to think about' is the most common reason a competent book stalls in the 60s. Re-derived 2026-08-26; being short bought it nothing.

t: Vrchol vulkanu (The Top of the Volcano)
why: Award-winning short SF with genuine per-story ideas, which survives the sharpened rule - but a self-selected career retrospective is uneven by construction, and the confrontational register carries real sexual-violence content on the axis that actually costs. Re-derived 2026-08-26.
Sequel to the two highest scores in the log (95, 92) with the protagonist already proven; discounted for the sequels-are-not-safe rule and Brown's own 95->92 slope.
Clears occult, worldbuilding and prophecy; Vin is a rootable lead with real interiority. Held under 90 by heavy exposition and an ideas ceiling.
One declared premise, society as subject, consequences worked out - the Hunger Games 89 shape. Juliette is motive-driven. Bleak but relieved, a mild pushback only.

t: Leva ruka tmy (The Left Hand of Darkness)
why: Society as subject with one declared premise - ambisexual humans on a glacial world - worked out through politics, language and religion, and the occult check passed 2026-08-26 (no spellcasting; the Earthsea objection does not scope to her Hainish work). Risks are the glacial-trek bleakness and a contemplative pace.
Short idea-driven with society as subject and a lead who has real interiority - the Animal Farm 78 / Little Prince 82 profile, where the character rules are suspended anyway.

Yarvi is a maimed prince driven by a vow - motive-forward, the axis that outranks worldbuilding. Declares little supernatural so little binds it, and far cleaner than First Law. Teen lead is a couple of points.

The strongest form-one case in the library - one premise, consequences over millennia, the PHM 92 profile. NOT predicted up on that: the spider strand has no one to root for and protagonist outranks worldbuilding, which is the Artemis error.
Testimony about what is true - the Qureshi 91 pattern, not the bare form Anne Frank 40 discredited. Risks are camp bleakness (mild) and a theory-heavy back half that edges toward theory-as-subject.

The same author's Little Prince scored 82 and these carry the same reflective register, with real ideas about duty, solitude and what men owe each other. Kept high on the author's proven record rather than on the form; trimmed slightly because the form itself no longer adds.

Heavy interiority and a staggered chapter-per-POV opening, both confirmed acceptable. Two live risks: First Law's crude sexual material (the axis that actually costs, and the 'only occasional' defence is void), and rootability - Glokta is a torturer, which is the Ballad 65 failure mode. Field fix 2026-08-26: axis:protagonist appeared in both leanedOn and risks, which makes both fields useless; it is kept as the axis carrying the number and the range already expresses the uncertainty. No number changed.
Single legible first-person with personhood as its idea, and short enough to sit in the idea-driven category. Access is the open question, not fit.

A single protagonist in first person with a want the whole plot runs on - the axis that outranks worldbuilding whenever the two compete (Artemis 69) - and a declared power system the society is visibly organised around: ceding will buys status, so the hierarchy is a consequence of the rule rather than decoration. That is the declared-capability test passed, the axis Hunger Games 89 and Ender's Game 87 both score on. Prophecy machinery is the graded risk, judged on reverence rather than resemblance - Narnia 67 keeps Aslan without objection. Access is the constraint, not fit.

Canonical short SF, and individual stories will land well. But an anthology has no single idea to name and averages toward its middle, so there is nothing to predict it up on: the short-form suspension removes penalties and never adds points, and canonicity is not a positive case (Animal Farm 78 and The Little Prince 82 earn on their ideas, not their status). The real argument is cheap breadth across a dozen authors, which is a reason to read it next rather than a reason to expect a high score. Re-derived 2026-08-26.

One strong nameable idea - a community that abolished pain, choice and colour, and what inheriting its memories costs - with the premise followed through. Survives the sharpened rule; trimmed because the YA register and the child lead are now unoffset.

PROVISIONAL - contents unverified, and the sharpened rule means an unverified short collection can no longer be floated on the category alone. Sanderson clears occult, worldbuilding and prophecy, but clearing filters is not a positive case. Wide range because the contents genuinely decide it; check the shelf before proposing.

The strongest worldbuilding case available - one invented drive and the whole civilisation reorganises around water, air and g-tolerance - and two anchored POVs, so the opening clears. Wide range because half the book is Miller working a missing-person case, adjacent to the one hard-avoided genre.
A society that has abolished death and must administer it - premise declared and followed through. YA register and teen leads are small pushbacks.

Declares less than Mistborn does, so less binds it, and the Defiant caste order does follow from the war. Drags: YA register, teen pilot lead, training-school structure - a lower ceiling than Mistborn but no English needed.

Essence precisely declared and the society built around it. The chosen-one plot is only a graded deduction (corrected 2026-08-22). Held down by a generic lead and a school opening; open risk is whether the sacrificial arc runs close to a Christ parallel.
Short, first-person, legible from page one, collapse premise worked out. Low ceiling but the lowest risk on the list - narrow range on purpose.

Anchored on Monte Cristo 75 from the same author: historical, so reality binds, but loose with history without stating false claims as fact. Vivid ensemble and the same momentum; digression is the only real drag.

Undertakes to explain and honours it - the park declares its control rules and the plot is those rules failing as declared. Not predicted up on that: functional thin characters and a set-piece second half are the Artemis shape.

Runs on banking and grain rather than battle, so it is motive-forward by construction - page time on what people want and why, the axis Mockingjay 91 tops the log on - and no strand of it is an investigation, so the hard filter stays clear. Sprawling and slow is the cost: a thin story spread over many pages is the density penalty that capped LOTR 84 and docked Monte Cristo 75. Ideas are the second risk - the politics are absorbing while they run, and there may be nothing to take away afterwards.

Canon and idea-dense, and the range assumes the opening holds. Re-derived 2026-08-28: it probably does not, and that is no longer a caveat. In medias res with unexplained jargon is the hard clarity filter, and that exact configuration has now been read and scored - Caropisci 30, abandoned in chapter one, a heist already running whose invented vocabulary and factions arrived unexplained, on a book that was the strongest unread SF-F pick on the shelf when it was proposed. Gibson does the same thing harder and on purpose, and the disorientation is the point rather than a threshold to cross. The number is unchanged because the range is conditional on the risk not firing, and averaging a hard filter into a hedge is what this file forbids: this is a 75 or a 30, not a 55. What changed is the probability, and the Author row is now Avoid-unless-asked rather than Revisit.

t: Pilire zeme (The Pillars of the Earth)
why: The plot is a multi-decade saga of building a cathedral against political intrigue, war and family betrayal, not a sexual relationship, so the sex-as-the-plot filter does not fire. The consequence-worked cathedral-building plot and multi-character motive structure are a real positive case, comparable to the historical-epic band this reader has liked: Count of Monte Cristo 75, Les Miserables 71, Exodus 68, Quo Vadis 66. Held at this range on 2026-08-28 with the comparator corrected. Ruled 2026-08-28: The Witcher 53 is a CONFOUNDED row and cannot be cited as a sexual-axis floor - the reader named two independent causes, 'both magic (witches) and the sex was through out the series', and the magic is the occult filter, the most severe objection in the log. The clean crudeness anchor is Ready Player One 55 - 'it was the kind of sex that reduced it that much', the kind and not the amount - with Artemis 69 confirming crudeness costs even in small doses. VOLUME IS UNANCHORED and must not be priced as cheap: Red Rising 95 and Valka stareho muze 87 are BOTH low volume on the reader's own account ('mostly one chapter of a book'), so neither shows what sustained non-crude content costs, and the log's only high-volume row is the confounded one. Note also that VSM's single chapter was still enough to become his one named complaint, so light volume is not free. The correction does not rescue this book, because the dimension it downgrades is not the one doing the work here: the treatment is described as fixated on the mechanics of rape to the point of being gratuitous, which is the crudeness dimension at its worst and is the Ready Player One charge at far greater length. Volume then compounds it rather than causing it.

t: Naslouchej nozi (The Knife of Never Letting Go)
why: One declared premise - audible thoughts - worked out consistently. Risk is the stylised dialect first-person opening: legible but unusual, and clarity is the hard filter. Teen lead and grimness are small pushbacks. Field fix 2026-08-26: axis:opening appeared in both leanedOn and risks, which makes both fields useless; it is kept as the axis carrying the number and the range already expresses the uncertainty. No number changed.

The LitRPG game-mechanics ideas are real - a dungeon run as a televised system with declared rules that the plot then obeys - and they keep this off the floor of the C band. But a mid-70s ceiling built on ideas alone cannot survive this much crude sexual content stacked on top. Held on 2026-08-28 with the comparator corrected. Ruled 2026-08-28: The Witcher 53 is a CONFOUNDED row and cannot be cited as a sexual-axis floor - the reader named two independent causes, 'both magic (witches) and the sex was through out the series', and the magic is the occult filter, the most severe objection in the log. The clean crudeness anchor is Ready Player One 55 - 'it was the kind of sex that reduced it that much', the kind and not the amount - with Artemis 69 confirming crudeness costs even in small doses. VOLUME IS UNANCHORED and must not be priced as cheap: Red Rising 95 and Valka stareho muze 87 are BOTH low volume on the reader's own account ('mostly one chapter of a book'), so neither shows what sustained non-crude content costs, and the log's only high-volume row is the confounded one. Note also that VSM's single chapter was still enough to become his one named complaint, so light volume is not free. The Ready Player One half of the old comparison is the half that applies, and it applies directly: pervasive, graphic and crude at once is that charge at greater length.

Reopened 2026-08-31 on Mort 83: the prose-style discount this line carried is gone, so the range rises from [70, 79] and this is a real proposal rather than a retest. Ideas carry it - a boy and a girl rebuilding a wiped-out island nation, with whether the gods exist and what makes a people the declared subject, worked out rather than asserted, which is the earner behind Animal Farm 78 and The Little Prince 82 and the thing Narnia 67 was marked down for lacking; belief stays a thread inside a survival story rather than becoming the subject, so it sits on the right side of the faith preference. Opening verdict: one concrete situation the reader has the context to read - a wave, an emptied island, one survivor - with no invented vocabulary to decode, the opposite of the roughly six simultaneous thread starts that produced The Colour of Magic 30 and Guards! Guards! 30, and it is the same authorial voice that scored 83. World verdict: a near-real-world alternate 1860s Pacific with nothing supernatural declared as a mechanism, so reality binds and it holds; the alternate British succession is a device and is the one thin spot on the fact face. Risks: the YA crossover register, which costs heavily only where there is no adult layer to grade and here there is one; and the lead, who spends the first stretch in grief and acted upon rather than wanting something, the Oliver Twist 57 exposure. Ceiling is the comic-fantasy A band rather than above it - Hitchhiker's Guide 83 and Saturnin 78 both score on voice and character - with one nameable idea set on top of that.
Accessible and funny with a legible single voice, but easy-but-shallow is a known mid-70s ceiling. Access is the constraint, not fit.

Light comic standalone with clear prose and a legible opening - a Hollywood agent hired to represent the first aliens to make contact, one situation stated on page one. RAISED 2026-08-28 on a real score rather than a guess: Valka stareho muze 87 confirms the prose is clear and the openings legible, and retires the 'nothing to think about, ceiling near 70' worry that held the old range down. It does not transfer wholesale - that book earned its 87 on a worked-out premise and an alien culture taken seriously, and this is a comedy with a slighter idea, which is the Hitchhiker's Guide 83 shape at a lower altitude. The top assumes the comic voice carries it; the floor is the competent-but-thin B band.
Worldbuilding fails on form two: it undertakes to explain in real quantum vocabulary, so real physics binds it, and it handles that loosely. Thriller pacing carries it but it is thin on motive.

Momentum and a premise stated plainly - memory as a place you can go back to - and the motive engine is unusually clear for a thriller: a father who lost a daughter, a scientist whose mother is losing herself, each wanting one thing for the whole book. That is what holds it in the B band. The deduction is the second form of the heaviest axis: Crouch undertakes to explain the mechanism in real vocabulary, so the explanation becomes binding, and the rules bend to suit each act rather than holding under thought. Access is the constraint as well.

BLOCKED on the occult depiction test: the divinities are invented so the source test passes, but miracles are rituals learned and performed on the page by Shara and Sigrud. Hard filter, so no estimate is carried. Evidence is fan-wiki and review level - strong enough to drop, weak enough to revisit if the reader disagrees.

Czech original, so no translation route needed. The whole book is why Hana became who she is - the motives axis directly, which is the axis that separates Mockingjay 91 from Catching Fire 83. Historical, so reality binds, and the 1954 typhus epidemic it turns on is real and researched: the fact face passes. Set in the reader's own town. Risks: Holocaust plus epidemic is heavy, and the first section is narrated by a child.

Genuinely idea-dense: the 20th century told as a flat catalogue of its own statistics and atrocities, which is an argument about how the century narrated itself. Survives the sharpened rule on that. But it has no protagonist and no narrative line, and the deadpan accumulation is a structural and bleakness risk rather than a free pass. Re-derived 2026-08-26.

Short novella whose whole plot is a con - a group paying for a rescue that was never going to happen - so it is built on weighing what is believable, the rigour credited for Seeking Allah 91. Risk: unrelieved bleakness, and the Anne Frank 40 precedent shows the Holocaust subject earns nothing by itself.

Four narrators, staggered rather than simultaneous, so the opening still clears, and the political material - expulsion, penal labour, a friend's crisis of faith - is idea-dense in the way that lifts a book out of the 60s. But the revenge plot's climax is an extended, weighted seduction scene, not a brief or incidental one, and the corrected axis prices that length and explicitness on their own terms - coldness of tone is not the same as it being restrained or small in volume, which is what the previous note assumed when it called the treatment clinical and left the axis unpriced. The essayistic digressions remain a separate, smaller density penalty in the Les Miserables 71 mould.

Screened and recorded low rather than dropped, because it fails on a graded axis, not a filter. First-person slow descent into evil with nobody to root for - the exact Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes 65 shape, which cost 22 points against Sunrise 87 on the protagonist alone. Being short and idea-driven (how a mild man becomes a monster) is the only thing holding it this high. Field fix 2026-08-26: axis:protagonist appeared in both leanedOn and risks, which makes both fields useless; it is kept as the axis carrying the number and the range already expresses the uncertainty. No number changed.

Psychohistory is declared precisely and the entire book is its consequences playing out over centuries - form one and form two both engaged, and the Empire's decline is genuinely reorganised around it. Almost all of it is people talking and scheming rather than acting, which is the Mockingjay 91 / Speaker 90 axis. Deliberately NOT leaned on worldbuilding, because the lead is not thin so much as absent - each section jumps decades to a new cast. Silmarillion 80 is the controlled case that says no-protagonist is survivable when the work is idea-driven; the risk is that the episodes read as unconnected, which is the Unfinished Tales 69 structure face.

The closest axis match in the whole score-5 batch. One premise declared precisely - surgery raises an IQ of 68 - and the whole book is its consequences, including the reversal, so form one and form two are both discharged. Told as Charlie's own progress reports, which makes motives the only content there is, and he is both interesting and worth rooting for, the pairing that separates Speaker 90 from Artemis 69. Bleakness is real but declines gradually rather than arriving as a twist, which is the mild-pushback shape, not the Ballad 65 shape. A second print translation exists (Lucie Bohemia 2011, Richard Podany) if the Knizni klub edition is out.

A dust-cruiser sinks in a lunar sea and the rest is engineering under a clock - the Project Hail Mary 92 shape, competence and physics worked out rather than asserted. Clarke declares the dust's behaviour and then obeys it for 250 pages, which is the worldbuilding axis in its purest form. Small cast, one thread, no prophecy, no occult. The risk is Clarke's habitual thinness of character; here it is mitigated because the trapped passengers' motives are the drama.

Unspace is declared with rules and the rules are then what the plot runs on - a declared capability whose consequences the book actually carries, the axis Project Hail Mary 92 and Ender's Game 87 both score on. Idris is the reason not to lean on the world alone: an Intermediary with a concrete want and a cost he keeps paying, so the Artemis 69 trap of predicting up on worldbuilding over a thin lead does not apply on the evidence. The floor drops on re-derivation though, because Artemis was revised down on 2026-08-27: the penalty for the protagonist risk firing is now measurably worse than it looked, and this range is conditional on that risk not firing. The other risk is the ensemble of crew POVs - they braid in after Idris is established rather than starting at once, which is the LOTR 84 pattern and not the Guards! Guards! 30 one, but there are enough of them to matter.

t: Muz, ktery si pletl manzelku s kloboukem (The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat)
why: Hits the non-fiction earner exactly as the profile states it: examining what is actually true, plus insight into how another group experiences the world. Anne Frank 40 failed because bare testimony earns nothing; Sacks is the opposite case, every chapter a short idea-driven piece with a nameable question. Case-study form means the character rules are suspended without needing the suspension. Density is the only risk - the neurological apparatus can crowd the story out. A sibling volume surfaced in the same query and is unassessed: Antropolozka na Marsu, Portal 2025.

Short, single-protagonist, one idea declared and worked out to its end - that wisdom cannot be transmitted, only lived. That is the The Little Prince 82 shape at the higher end, because the idea is harder and the protagonist actually changes rather than serving as a vehicle for it. Motives are the entire text. On the occult filter: asceticism and meditation are practised on the page but no deity is petitioned and nothing supernatural is enacted, so it does not fire. Faith is the graded risk instead - what the profile wants is religion carried inside a story (Seeking Allah 91, Son of Hamas 75) rather than as a subject in its own right, and this sits close to that boundary.

Fiction doing the thing that earned Seeking Allah 91 and Son of Hamas 75: insight into how another group experiences the world, from inside. Guilt and its attempted repair is the engine, so page time goes to what Amir wants and why rather than what he does. Flawed-but-rootable lead, single thread, clear opening. The risk is severity rather than bleakness of tone - there is a child rape and it is not softened; the treatment is serious rather than crude, which is the axis that matters here, but it is the one thing that could sink this below the range.

A meteor strike in 1952 forces the space programme early, and the book actually reorganises its society around that declaration rather than asserting it once - the worldbuilding obligation discharged. Elma is a computer and a pilot, so competence is earned rather than granted, which is where Artemis 69 lost points. Her anxiety disorder is where the motives live. Volume 1, correct entry point.

Alternate-history space programme with a first-person lead who has a concrete job to do and a private illness to hide - motives on the page rather than set-piece action, the axis Mockingjay 91 tops the log on. Two deductions hold it in the low 70s. It is a sequel, and sequels are not safe bets: Hitchhiker's 83 to 70 is the steepest fall in the log, so nothing is inherited from a predecessor. And the plot is a sabotage hunt - not a detective novel, but investigation is its structure, which is close enough to a hard filter that it must be said out loud before this is ever proposed.

Ninety pages, one protagonist, and the private humiliation is what drives the public act - motives over action with nothing else in the way, which is the axis Mockingjay 91 tops the log on. The idea is nameable in a phrase, so the short form is not what is carrying it. Deliberately not leaned on protagonist: Milos is interesting throughout but only becomes rootable at the end. Bleakness is a mild pushback at most - Animal Farm 78 is bleak and pays nothing for it. An audio edition exists (Supraphon 2009, Krystof Hadek) alongside four print ones.

Seldon is on the page from the first chapter to the last, so psychohistory arrives as one man's problem rather than as scaffolding the reader is told about - a continuous protagonist with a concrete want, which is the axis that outranks worldbuilding whenever the two compete (Artemis 69). Held in the low 70s because this is late Asimov writing backwards into work he had already finished: the ideas are retrofitted rather than generative, and Trantor is toured more than it is worked out. Density is the second risk - long stretches of guided tour rather than plot.

One premise - an outpatient procedure that makes couples emotionally telepathic - and Willis takes its social consequences seriously enough that the comedy comes out of the rules rather than around them. That is the worldbuilding axis being paid rather than dodged. Rootable lead, single thread, clear opening. Risk is Willis's screwball method: farce runs on interruption and missed connection, and 500 pages of it is where the thin-story-spread-thin penalty would land. Romance is central but not the point and is not crudely handled.

Leaves ideas behind, which is the profile's own phrase, and the HAL section is pure motive - why a machine that cannot lie starts lying. Clarke's physics is declared and kept. Two deductions: nobody in it is rootable, and the last act deliberately stops explaining after the book has spent 200 pages explaining everything, which is the undertook-to-explain breach rather than the vague-magic exemption. Odeon 1982 is the older print route if the Argo edition is out.

t: Ozvena veci budoucich (An Echo of Things to Come)
why: A declared magic system whose costs are actually paid, and leads who keep concrete wants through a much larger plot - declared rules working as an asset rather than as an unmet obligation. Held rather than raised for two reasons. The prophecy machinery gets heavier in this volume, and prophecy is graded on reverence rather than resemblance - Aslan is the closest Christ figure there is and is not among Narnia 67's objections, while careless resonance costs - and that cannot be verified from outside the book. And sequels are not safe bets in this log: Hitchhiker's 83 to 70.

The idea is nameable in a phrase - whether a nation that has forgotten its atrocity should be made to remember - and the mist is a declared mechanism the book obeys. Axl and Beatrice are a rootable pair with one clear want. The dragon and the ogres are invented, so the occult filter does not fire. Risk is pace: Ishiguro writes it deliberately flat and dreamlike, which is the closest thing here to heavy description with little story in it.

Two hundred pages narrated by a foetus who overhears his mother plotting his father's murder - one conceit, declared on page one, obeyed throughout, which is the short idea-driven category at its safest. The killers' motives are the whole content. On the detective filter: the reader knows who and why from the start, so this is the inverse of a mystery, not an instance of one. Risk is that the narrator physically cannot act, and a protagonist with no agency is a thinner proposition than a thin protagonist.

Motives over action is not a feature of this book, it is the method - almost nothing happens except people calculating, and Cromwell is both interesting and, unusually for him, rootable. Historical fiction lands fine for this reader (Quo Vadis 66, Exodus 68) and this is far better written than either. The opening is the real risk and it is a genuine one: Mantel writes an unsignalled 'he' for Cromwell and drops a large Tudor cast in without introduction, which is a different failure from simultaneous threads but produces the same first-chapter confusion that ended Mortal Engines 55.

One premise stated plainly - every unlived life is a book you can try - with a rootable lead and a nameable idea, read quickly. Risk is on the heaviest axis: the library's rules are thin and Haig leans on them constantly, which is exactly the combination the profile penalises (obligation scales with how hard the book leans, not what it is about). If the rules turn out to bend for the plot this drops into the 60s.

A mother searching for the child taken from her - one want stated plainly and pursued for the whole book, the motives-over-action axis at its most direct (Mockingjay 91). Held below the A band because the engine is the search rather than a single idea worked out, and this log pays for ideas above emotion: Animal Farm 78 and The Little Prince 82 both earn on an idea nameable in a phrase, and this one is 'find the child'. Sequels are not safe bets either - Hitchhiker's 83 to 70. Life-phase proximity is a small pushback at most, never a tier.

A single monologue by a man reconstructing why his wife killed herself: motives are not a feature of the text, they are the text - the axis Mockingjay 91 and Speaker for the Dead 90 both score on, in fifty pages. The idea is nameable and it is the whole book, so the short form is not carrying it. Bleakness is a mild pushback rather than a filter; 1984 60 is the only book in the log grim enough to have cost real points.

The Petersburg tales - a clerk's diary sliding into madness, a nose with a career of its own. Each piece has an idea nameable in a phrase, which is the bar the short-form rule sets, and it clears that bar on the ideas rather than on being short: the suspension removes penalties (The Little Prince 82's child lead, Animal Farm 78's bleakness) and never adds points. Held under the A band because the pieces do not build on each other, a light version of the Unfinished Tales 69 objection, and because there is nobody in them to root for. Audio edition also exists (Supraphon 2015).

Re-derived 2026-08-27 against a real score by this author. Promena 58 is the measurement that matters: the same author, the same very short form, and the same two risks - a passive lead who is hard to root for, and bleakness that arrives at once instead of gradually - and both fired, taking it twelve points below what was predicted for it. This story is thinner still: one scene, and the verdict is asserted rather than worked out, so the short-form suspension removes penalties without adding anything. Leaning on the protagonist axis rather than on ideas now, because that is what carried the number down in the read book; the idea is kept in risks because the single image may yet land. Below Divergent 58 at the low end and under Percy Jackson 57 is the honest floor for a device narrator with nothing to root for.

One idea declared and carried the whole way without flinching, in 120 pages, and it is nameable in a sentence. The deduction is the protagonist: Meursault is built not to be rootable, which is the Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes 65 failure - 22 points under Sunrise on the Reaping 87 on that axis alone, same author, same world. The idea payload is what holds this in the 70s rather than the 60s. Print routes are Garamond 2009 (bilingual) and Mlada fronta 1966, plus a Tympanum audiobook.

Reverent allegory is explicitly fine and the ideas are the entire architecture, so nothing here is filtered - but the range is wide because density decides it. Fourteen thousand lines of terza rima carrying fourteenth-century Florentine politics that only footnotes can unlock is the Bidnici 71 penalty at several times the dose. Mikes (Academia 2009) is the readable modern translation; Vrchlicky (Dobrovsky 2013) is not. Reached from the Ukrainian-language score-5 row Bozestvenna komedija, which is not a route.

The idea is good and nameable - a monument on Pluto whose origin nobody can prove, and history as something arguable rather than known. Structure is the risk: three sections, three casts, centuries apart, and no protagonist survives the gaps. The Tolkien pair prices exactly that shape - Silmarillion 80 shows it is survivable when the ideas carry the book, Unfinished Tales 69 shows the cost when the parts stop connecting to each other - and Robinson's sections connect coldly and loosely, which is why this sits nearer the bottom of its range.

t: Jonathan Strange & pan Norrell (Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell)
why: BLOCKED on the occult filter 2026-08-26, when the reader ruled that failing EITHER test is a veto. Raising a dead woman and striking the bargain with the gentleman with the thistle-down hair are both performed on the page, with no mechanical account of either, and English magic is spellcasting in the historical-occult mould. This estimate's own why argued the opposite - 'an invented system inside an alternate England, and invented magic is explicitly fine' - which is exactly the reading retired on 2026-08-26.

t: Neviditelny zivot Addie LaRue (The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue)
why: A bargain with an invented entity, whose terms - nobody can remember her, she cannot say her own name or leave a mark - are declared precisely. That precision is the risk rather than the strength: the profile says rules add obligation, not bonus, and this book is widely argued to bend its own. Addie is rootable and the want is clear. Sexual content is present and treated seriously rather than crudely, which is the axis that matters, but it is central enough to name. Re-examined against the occult ruling of 2026-08-26 (failing EITHER test is a veto, and a rite enacted on the page fails even when the system is invented): the record does not settle it, so the number is unchanged but axis:occult is now a priced risk rather than a cleared question - this range is void if the check below fails. Outstanding check: a bargain with a dark entity struck on the page - the Jonathan Strange ruling treated a faerie bargain as a rite, so this needs the same test.

t: Dvanact povidek o poutnicich (Doce cuentos peregrinos)
why: The stories are built on situations rather than on atmosphere, and several have an idea statable in a phrase - the bar the short-form rule sets, since the suspension removes penalties and never adds points. Marked as a risk on exactly that: in the weaker half the idea dissolves into mood, and short and elegant earns nothing on its own (Animal Farm 78 and The Little Prince 82 are canonical for their ideas, not for their length). Audio edition also exists (Tympanum 2013).

First-person throughout, and moral autonomy against every pressure is a real idea carried by a genuinely rootable narrator - the two things the profile weights most. What keeps it here rather than higher is that the middle third is a sustained romance with the Gothic apparatus around it, and the Moor House section stalls badly. Not filtered on sexual treatment; there is nothing to filter. Covers the duplicate score-5 rows Jana Eyrova (Alpress 2007, Fastrova) and Jane Eyrova (this record); the CooBoo 2019 edition is abridged and is not a route.

t: Starec, ktery cetl milostne romany (Un viejo que leia novelas de amor)
why: A hundred and thirty pages, one setting, one old man, and a clean line about what outsiders do to a place they do not understand. Same bracket as Racek 64-74 and for the same reason: the form is safe, the idea is real but slight, and slightness is what caps it. The title is not what it looks like - the romances are a running joke, not the subject.

The subject is exactly the reader's kind of subject - how a rebellion turns on the people who made it - and the silkpunk world is invented with rules. The method is the problem. Liu writes it in the manner of a dynastic chronicle: omniscient, distant, characters described from outside rather than inhabited, and a cast that keeps widening from the first chapters. That is the opening filter in both its shapes at once - too many lines opened before any is established, and no vantage point from which the reader can tell why any of them matters - and it defeats the protagonist axis at the same time. It is deliberate rather than a flaw, so it will not improve on page fifty. Caropisci 30 is why this is priced hard rather than flagged softly: that book also opened on plenty of incident, and incident without context is what he walked out on. Re-examined against the occult ruling of 2026-08-26 (failing EITHER test is a veto, and a rite enacted on the page fails even when the system is invented): the record does not settle it, so the number is unchanged but occult is a priced risk rather than a cleared question, and this range is void if that check fails. Outstanding check: the gods intervene directly - is any invocation staged on the page?

Genuinely conflicted, and recorded here rather than proposed because of it. Orogeny is declared with real costs and the whole civilisation is organised around it - the declared-capability test passed as thoroughly as in the log's own positives, Hunger Games 89 and Ender's Game 87, and Hugo-winning besides. Against that, the opening is the exact configuration the reader hard-filters on: three named threads braided from chapter one, one of them in second person, with in-world vocabulary used before it is explained. That is the Guards! Guards! 30 shape, and Mortal Engines 55 was abandoned on less. The threads do resolve into one person, but not for hundreds of pages, so the filter could fire long before the payoff. Anyone proposing this must lead with the opening, not with the awards.

t: General ve svem labyrintu (El general en su laberinto)
why: Bolivar's last river journey, so no magical realism and nothing for the occult filter - straight historical fiction about a man's motives as he loses everything. That is the right axis. The costs are that it assumes a reader who already knows the Gran Colombian collapse, and that the arc is unbroken decline with no counterweight.

t: Pohreb Velke matky (Los funerales de la Mama Grande)
why: Short form, which is the safe category, and the title piece has a real satirical idea. Two reasons it is recorded rather than proposed: several stories run on folk-Catholic supernatural treated as literally true, which is close to the occult filter without clearly tripping it - worth verifying before this is ever offered - and in the weaker pieces the content is atmosphere rather than idea.

These stories turn on a dread rather than on a premise, and a mood is not an idea you can name in a phrase - the bar the short-form rule sets, since the suspension removes penalties and never adds points. That is the whole reason for the low range: nothing is wrong with it and little is left behind, which is the Narnia 67 objection. The Elliott family pieces also put witchcraft on the page as family practice; it reads as invented rather than drawn from real occultism, so probably clear of the hard filter, but it needs checking rather than assuming. Re-examined against the occult ruling of 2026-08-26 (failing EITHER test is a veto, and a rite enacted on the page fails even when the system is invented): the record does not settle it, so the number is unchanged but axis:occult is now a priced risk rather than a cleared question - this range is void if the check below fails. Outstanding check: the Elliott family stories - flagged as needing a check since before this ruling and still unchecked.

t: Hvezdy jako prach (The Stars, Like Dust)
why: Early Asimov writing a chase with a conspiracy attached rather than a premise worked out, and he rated it his own weakest. The reveal it builds to - the document that will free the galaxy is the United States Constitution - costs on the heaviest axis instead of paying on it: a galaxy-scale claim asserted rather than earned, the Divergent 58 shape of ideas assembled without cohering. What keeps it out of the 50s is momentum, a real positive in this log (Hunger Games 89, Red Rising 95), and a lead with one clear want.

t: Sila psa (The Power of the Dog)
why: Motive-driven in the strict sense - the whole book is why Phil is cruel, and the answer is withheld and then earned. But the man whose head the reader lives in is repellent by design, which is the Ballad of Songbirds 65 shape that cost twenty-two points, and the Montana ranch is rendered at length with little happening in it. Sexual content is implicit throughout and handled seriously; that is not the deduction here.

t: Ministerstvo pro budoucnost (The Ministry for the Future)
why: An enormous idea payload and the worst delivery of it for this reader. A hundred-odd chapters, many of them essays, riddles or unattributed eyewitness fragments with no continuing character, and the opening throws several of these forms at once before any thread is established. That is the simultaneous-lines shape of the filter behind three 30s, and the fragments compound it with the second shape, since an unattributed eyewitness voice gives the reader no context to read itself by. The thin-story-spread-thin penalty arrives on top, with no protagonist to offset either - and the protagonist axis outranks whatever it competes with (Artemis 69). Recorded so it is not lost, not proposed.

A hundred and fifty pages, one conceit - anonymous admiring letters, and who we are to the person who loves us - and an ending that retroactively dissolves the plot. The idea is nameable in a phrase, which is what keeps this out of the 50s. Two deductions. The essayistic digressions are the Bidnici 71 penalty in miniature, where the non-plot material is what cost the points. And the erotic preoccupation is treated coldly and instrumentally throughout: not crude, so not a filter, but the same axis that took Artemis 69 down four points from its prediction. Audio edition also exists (Supraphon 2025).

The idea is first-rate and unusual - the American colonies before race had hardened into the thing it became - and Morrison is a better writer than most of this list. It is recorded low purely on the opening: several unnamed first-person voices in dialect, non-linear, with the reader expected to work out who is speaking. That is the filter's own description of what to avoid, and it is the first page rather than a later section.

Lyric vignettes of one summer with almost no plot: heavy description with little story in it, which is a stated deduction and the density penalty at its most concentrated - LOTR 84 was capped for a thin story spread over many pages, and that was with Tolkien's ideas set against it. Here there is no idea nameable in a phrase to set against anything, only nostalgia itself, so the short-form suspension does not apply and would not help if it did. Three print editions held.

The premise is good and the satire lands - a self-governing island of millionaires that tears itself apart over which half owns it - so there is an idea and it has consequences. Everything else is against it: the characters are a quartet of interchangeable musicians used as a camera, and Verne pads with inventory and itinerary, which is the heavy-description deduction.

Two interleaved storylines and both are extended seductions: an eighteenth-century chevalier's night-long, stage-by-stage seduction of a chatelaine at a chateau, and a modern academic's parallel pursuit of a woman at the same chateau turned hotel. The essays on speed, memory and forgetting are commentary layered onto those two narratives, not an independent plot of their own - strip out the two libertine episodes and there is no novel left to narrate, only essays. That is the plot being mainly a sexual pursuit in two historical registers, which the new premise test rejects regardless of the philosophical framing wrapped around it.

Short form, so the character and emotion rules are suspended - but the suspension only removes penalties. Chekhov's declared method is to pose and refuse to answer, which means there is deliberately no idea to carry away, and that is the exact case the profile scores a 3. Recorded so the Chekhov holdings do not keep resurfacing as canonical.

Fifteen stories built on paralysis and the withheld epiphany - eventless by design, and the withholding is the method, so there is deliberately no idea to carry away. That is the case the profile scores a 3: the short form suspends the character and emotion rules, but the suspension only removes penalties, and what earns is an idea left behind (Animal Farm 78, The Little Prince 82). The Dublin specificity adds a comprehension cost on top of that. Canonical and a poor fit; another of the rows that exposed the model's canon bias.

Technically superb domestic realism whose whole aim is a life glimpsed sideways - no premise, no consequences, nothing to think about afterwards, which is the profile's stated earner absent entirely. Nobel prestige is what scored it a 5 in triage, and exclusions are not credentials. Recorded low rather than rejected, because it fails on a graded axis and not on a filter.

t: Pritelkyne z mladi (Friend of My Youth)
why: Domestic realism carried by observation and reticence: nothing is declared, so nothing has to be worked out, and the interest is in what each story withholds. That is the least transferable thing on this reader's axes - what earns here is an idea left behind (Seeking Allah 91, Animal Farm 78, The Little Prince 82) and there is none to name. Recorded low rather than rejected: it fails on a graded axis, not a filter, and clearing the filters is never a reason to propose.

t: Nepritel, pritel, ctitel, milenec, manzel (Hateship, Friendship, Courtship, Loveship, Marriage)
why: Observation and reticence rather than premise and consequence - domestic realism with no idea to name at the end, and an idea left behind is what earns in this log (Seeking Allah 91, Animal Farm 78). Recorded low rather than rejected, because nothing here trips a hard filter. Worth noting that this row was machine-classed romance-maybe on its title alone and ranked -16, the lowest in the batch, while the model scored it 5: the two signals disagreed completely and both were wrong for different reasons.

Early experimental Hrabal: collage, no plot, no protagonist, and the interest is entirely in the sentence. That is the least transferable thing on this reader's axes - he wants motives on the page (Mockingjay 91) and an idea to take away (Animal Farm 78), and prose that refuses both offers neither. The opening is a real risk on top of that: a text with no legible starting situation is the failure behind three 30s. Also held as Brana 2001.

Anecdote and voice rather than premise and consequence - the monologues are collected for the talk itself, and there is no idea to name at the end of one, which is the bar the short-form rule sets. Nothing trips a hard filter, so this is recorded low rather than rejected. Route note - the only catalogue record under this title is the Popron 2006 audiobook read by Josef Somr and Magdalena Sidonova; the text is in print only inside Spisy 2 (Mlada fronta 2014). This row is also what exposed a bug in the access checker, which matched 'cte' but not 'ctou' and so read an audiobook as print.

Animal stories written for young readers, which is a small pushback rather than the children's filter - Seton wrote them for adults too and they are not simplified - but there is no premise being worked out and the emotional register is straightforwardly sentimental. Recorded low so it stops appearing as an unclassified canonical name.

Prose-poem fragments of a Banat childhood under Ceausescu, deliberately opaque, no plot and no argument - the Nobel citation is for the language. Heavy description with little story in it at maximum concentration, and the fragments do not connect to each other, which is the Unfinished Tales 69 objection. The totalitarian subject is the only thing keeping it off the floor, and the read pair that prices it is Animal Farm 78 against 1984 60: the subject earns when an idea is attached to it and costs when the book is only grim.

t: The City and Its Uncertain Walls
why: No route, and this is the reason it is here rather than in a proposal: the catalogue holds only the English Vintage hardback and no Czech translation exists yet for a 2025 novel. It reached the score-5 list because the pre-model foreign-edition filter was narrowed from 'vintage' to 'vintage books' when that substring was found to be matching Pistorius, so a bare Vintage imprint now slips through. On merit, first assessment of Murakami in this database and a sceptical one: the walled city is declared in detail and then deliberately never explained, which is the undertook-to-explain breach rather than the vague-magic exemption.

t: Inheritance, or, The Vault of souls
why: No route and wrong volume: the catalogue holds only the English Doubleday edition, and it is book four of four with the first three untracked. Recorded to close the row, not as a recommendation. The estimate is for the cycle rather than this volume - rule-bound magic in the ancient language, which pays the worldbuilding axis, against a heavily leaned-on chosen-one prophecy and a great deal of borrowed furniture. The live question this raises is volume 1, Eragon, whose Czech availability was not checked.

t: Neuveritelny a tklivy pribeh o bezelstne Erendire a jeji ukrutne babicce (The Incredible and Sad Tale of Innocent Erendira and Her Heartless Grandmother)
why: A short, fable-shaped novella with a nameable idea - a grandmother monetising her granddaughter's body as a debt, and what a person becomes under that arithmetic - told at fairy-tale distance rather than in the room. The content is grim but the treatment is serious rather than crude, which is the axis that docked Artemis 69, and it matches the 'serious rather than crude' reading already logged for Hosseini's child-rape scene. Held on 2026-08-28 with the comparator corrected, and the graded-crudeness axis added to deps - this line argued from that rule without depending on it. Ruled 2026-08-28: The Witcher 53 is a CONFOUNDED row and cannot be cited as a sexual-axis floor - the reader named two independent causes, 'both magic (witches) and the sex was through out the series', and the magic is the occult filter, the most severe objection in the log. The clean crudeness anchor is Ready Player One 55 - 'it was the kind of sex that reduced it that much', the kind and not the amount - with Artemis 69 confirming crudeness costs even in small doses. VOLUME IS UNANCHORED and must not be priced as cheap: Red Rising 95 and Valka stareho muze 87 are BOTH low volume on the reader's own account ('mostly one chapter of a book'), so neither shows what sustained non-crude content costs, and the log's only high-volume row is the confounded one. Note also that VSM's single chapter was still enough to become his one named complaint, so light volume is not free. The old text cited The Witcher 53 alongside Artemis as an axis this book clears; only the Artemis half of that was ever about this axis.

A nameable idea carried a long way: one early harm - the piano teacher's grooming of Roland from 11 to 14, escalating until he seeks her out to lose his virginity before what he believes will be nuclear war - and the book traces its consequence forward across the Cold War, the Wall and Covid, in the same declared-thing-and-its-consequences register the ideas axis credits Animal Farm 78 for. The opening is one concrete situation before it flashes back, so the confusing-opening filter does not fire, and there is no occult and no sustained investigation. This is not a single contained incident: it is one of the three relationships (alongside two marriages) the whole novel is structured around, recurring across the decades as the explanation for Roland's drifting adult life. Handled seriously does not zero this out the way the earlier note assumed - the corrected axis prices what is actually depicted on its own terms, not only how crude the prose register is, and a child's seduction by an adult carries real weight there even told in restrained, literary prose. What already capped this below Artemis 69 - a flatter, duller lead than Weir's - is compounded rather than relieved by this axis.

t: Muzi, kteri nemaji zeny (Men Without Women)
why: The collection's shared subject is men shaped by the absence or unknowability of women in their lives, not a sexual relationship as such, so filter 6 does not apply. But that subject is a mood, not a worked premise with consequences the way the ideas this reader rewards work (Project Hail Mary 92 on astrophage's second-order effects, Red Rising 95 on its interiority-driven plot) - a short story collection in literary fiction with a diffuse theme rather than a nameable, worked-out idea tends to settle in the low-to-mid 60s for this reader rather than climb into the A band. The sexual content itself is light in volume and restrained in explicitness, so it is a minor risk rather than what carries the number.

t: Prvni osoba jednotneho cisla (First Person Singular)
why: Eight first-person stories, mostly nostalgic reminiscence with one or two swerving into the fabulist (a talking monkey who steals women's names; an old man's riddle about a circle with no circumference). No hard filter fires: each story is single-narrator and legible from its first page, unlike the simultaneous-thread failures that scored 30; nothing on the page is real-world occultism, only invented strangeness; there is no investigation plot. On the heaviest axis Murakami sits outside the usual test rather than failing it: he never undertakes to explain the strange things he declares, and per the rule 'nothing obliges an author to explain anything,' an author who states up front that an event 'can't be explained, defies logic' is not reneging on a promise the way Mortal Engines or 2001 did - he never made one. That is a genuine difference from Chiang's Top-pick-candidate method of declaring one premise and rigorously working out its consequences: Murakami is close to the opposite of that discipline, so the worldbuilding axis gives him neither the Chiang-style credit nor a Mortal-Engines-style penalty - it is close to neutral here, not a driver of the score either way. What actually has to carry the number is whether the ideas left behind are good ones, per the short-idea-driven rule that the suspension of character/plot penalties never adds points by itself. Some stories clear that bar with a genuinely nameable idea - Cream's meditation on disturbing, unresolved experience losing its sting yet still shaping you; the title story and the memoir-blurring Yakult Swallows piece both worry at how solid a first-person self even is. But this is graded against real risk, not a clean pass: multiple reviews (Harvard Review's 'confusingly drawn map that means more to the creator than reader,' NPR's 'a few missteps... the payoff doesn't always satisfy') describe exactly the failure mode that downgraded Alice Munro - technique in search of a payoff that doesn't arrive - and Confessions of a Shinagawa Monkey is explicitly self-aware that it has no stated theme at all. That keeps this well short of Animal Farm 78 or The Little Prince 82, where the idea is sharp and singular, and lands it closer to the competent-but-uneven B band such as Les Miserables 71. Field fix 2026-08-26: axis:ideas appeared in both leanedOn and risks, which makes both fields useless; it is kept as the axis carrying the number and the range already expresses the uncertainty. No number changed.

t: Oci modreho psa (Ojos de perro azul)
why: Positive case: these eleven apprentice stories (written 1947-1955, collected 1974) run almost entirely on interior consciousness rather than event -- a boy narrates his own living burial from inside a coffin diagnosed as a 'living death', a woman narrates her wish to shed a hereditary curse of beauty by willing her soul into her cat -- which is the motives-over-action register that ranks Speaker for the Dead 90 and Mockingjay 91 above their more event-driven counterparts. Each story checked opens on one concrete, legible situation and stays there rather than fanning into several threads, the exact clarity that Gunslinger 30, Colour of Magic 30 and Guards! Guards! 30 all failed on. Deductions: this is an anthology, and per the anthology reasoning already on file, a collection has no single idea to name and averages toward its middle rather than being predictable up the way a single-premise work is. Critics treat these apprentice pieces as valuable mainly as a seed of the author's later style rather than as well-realized stories on their own, which is the heavy-description/thin-story shape that cost nothing in LOTR 84 but capped it at 84 rather than higher, and that is closer still to Unfinished Tales 69, 'fragmented and not aligned' -- eleven standalone, unconnected early pieces is nearer that shape than to one worked-through premise. Leaned on the anthology/ideas axis and the structural (fragmentation) face of worldbuilding, not on protagonist or opening clarity, both of which check out fine here and are not what caps this one. Field fix 2026-08-26: axis:worldbuilding appeared in both leanedOn and risks, which makes both fields useless; it is kept as the axis carrying the number and the range already expresses the uncertainty. No number changed.

The whole text is the narrator's own examination of what she wants and why, with almost no external action until the final page - a purer case of the axis that separates Mockingjay 91 from Catching Fire 83 and PHM 92 from The Martian 82, since here the ratio of interiority to event is even more extreme than either. The idea is nameable: seventeen sleepless days strip away a stereotyped, outwardly content marriage and let her see her own routine from outside, in the same short-idea-driven register as Animal Farm 78 (bleak, but leaves something to think about rather than immersing in misery) rather than the plain-warm register of The Little Prince 82. Two deductions keep it off the top: the ending leaves her alone in her car at night, unable to move, as two shadowy men rock the vehicle - unresolved and frightening rather than a settled resolution, so bleakness and the passive, uncertain final beat both cost a few points, the same way Artemis 69's flat-but-competent lead capped Weir's range even with the world-logic fine throughout. Leaned on motives-over-action first and the named idea second; not leaned on worldbuilding, since Murakami declares the anomaly (no sleep, no decline, if anything she looks younger) but never undertakes to explain its mechanism - the same protection that let Silmarillion 80 and Little Prince 82 carry unexplained strangeness with no penalty.

Reversalism - an inverted economy where workers pay their employer and shops pay customers - is nameable in a sentence, so it clears the bar the short-idea-driven rule sets before crediting a short book at all. But naming the gimmick is not the same as it holding up: reviewers report that once Reversalism is defined the novella stalls rather than working out its consequences with the rigor Project Hail Mary 92 (astrophage's second-order effects) or Golden Son 92 (earned reveals) show, and flag internal inconsistencies McEwan never resolves - a cockroach hive-mind remembering a human pop song, and a transformation that reads as an accident on the opening pages but a deliberate hivemind plan by the close. That is the heaviest-axis failure this reader's own rule names: the author must follow the rules he lays down, and here the premise does not survive its own book. Jim Sams is also not a protagonist worth rooting for - a satire vehicle standing in for a Boris Johnson figure, driven by cockroach appetite rather than any want-and-why - the same unrootable-lead problem that cost The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes 22 points against Sunrise on the Reaping, and the protagonist axis outranks worldbuilding when the two conflict. With the idea failing to hold under its own logic and no lead to invest in, there is no positive case here beyond having cleared the filters, which the rules explicitly say is not a case at all. That places it with Divergent 58 and Mortal Engines 55 - thin premise, no rootable lead - rather than with the short books that actually earned their score, Animal Farm 78 and The Little Prince 82. Field fix 2026-08-26: axis:ideas appeared in both leanedOn and risks, which makes both fields useless; it is kept as the axis carrying the number and the range already expresses the uncertainty. No number changed.

The Czech title tracks this book's spine more than the English 'Vagabond' does: Thomas is captured and interrogated by a Dominican inquisitor pursuing the Vexille heresy, which puts his stated Christian faith under real pressure instead of leaving it as backstory - the same 'does the book examine what is actually true' test that made Seeking Allah, Finding Jesus (91) the strongest testimony in the log, though here it is one thread inside an adventure plot, not the whole book, so it earns less than that memoir does. His friendship with the Scottish noble Robbie Douglas gives the loyalty-under-pressure axis Red Rising and Golden Son both score well on. Risk: this is the middle volume of an unresolved trilogy, so the Grail's declared power and the Vexille conspiracy's coherence cannot be graded yet, and Cornwell's usual thin-secondary-character problem still applies to the cast around the siege of La Roche-Derrien.

This is the one Sharpe entry in the batch not built around a battle: Sharpe investigates why his depleted regiment's replacements never arrived and uncovers a recruiting-fraud ring reaching into Whitehall, trading the series' usual set-piece for exactly the axis the log rewards most - what people want and why, worked out in scheme and consequence. Reviewers single this book out for its 'clever detail' and its departure from formula. Sharpe stays a rootable underdog defending his men against institutional betrayal, a milder version of the class-conflict idea that lifts this above the other three Sharpe entries here. Risk: the antagonists (Lord Fenner and the London 'nest of vipers') are reviewer-described in the same single-dimensional-villain terms that recur across the series, so this does not reach the tighter causal payoff of Golden Son's reveals (92).

A hundred-year-old man joins a flight to a comet and a second ship comes down on an ice moon: the sights are the point and the story is not. Reviewers converge on no path and no purpose, on long stretches of recycled text padding the length, and on the stranded crew never being in real danger - which removes the one thing that kept a survival story moving for this reader (The Martian 82 ran on problem-solving under threat). A thin story spread over pages is the penalty term in this log, the reason LOTR 84 could not pull clear of The Hobbit 84. Characterisation is the recurring complaint, and interiority is the axis that makes the difference at the top here - Red Rising 95 above Golden Son 92 on nothing else. Ideas belong in the risks, not the case for the book: the central mystery is barely advanced and reviewers report learning nothing new, so the one thing that could have carried a plotless book is the thing least likely to hold. A sequel as well, and sequels are not safe bets here - Hitchhiker's fell 83 to 70. Decided at the low-line gate on form, genre and one search.

t: 3001: posledni vesmirna odysea (3001: The Final Odyssey)
why: The premise is a good one and it is delivered on for a while: an astronaut left for dead is revived a thousand years later, and the first stretch is a guided tour of what changed, told through one man learning it. What sinks the number is exactly what this log punishes hardest. Reviewers agree on the shape - the tour is the strong part, the story after it is thinner still, and the resolution arrives in about a chapter. A thin story spread over pages is the standing penalty: LOTR 84 was held level with The Hobbit 84 because the story was very thin for the number of pages, and The Martian 82 was docked for an ending that dragged. The people are described as glossed over, and page time on what characters want and why is the axis that puts Mockingjay 91 and Speaker for the Dead 90 at the top. Ideas go in the risks rather than the leanedOn on purpose: the long-running mystery is finally answered by turning the mysterious thing into a machine that can be handed a computer virus, and a payoff like that leaves nothing behind. It is also a sequel, and sequels are not safe bets here - Hitchhiker's fell 83 to 70. Decided at the low-line gate on form, genre and one search; no deeper research would move it above 68.

t: A zrodi se Nadace (Forward the Foundation)
why: One man's life from forty to eighty-one, and the page time goes to what he wants and what it costs him rather than to events: the wife destroyed defending him, the adopted son killed, the funding stripped year by year, and the work continued anyway. That is the axis Speaker for the Dead at 90 and Mockingjay at 91 both top, motives and understanding over action, and it is unusual for this author to hand a book one figure to follow for its whole length. It also opens on a single legible situation, a middle-aged department head eight years into an academic post, with nothing running alongside it. Deducted for structure: four self-contained sections a decade apart, and Unfinished Tales at 69 is docked for exactly that complaint, pieces not connected to each other, though here one life does connect them. Deducted mildly for sustained decline, since the whole book is a civilisation coming apart and 1984 at 60 marks how depressing reads here. Leaned on the protagonist rather than on ideas, because the central theory is assumed in this book rather than argued and what is actually examined is a man running out of time. The mind-reading is an invented psychic talent, not occult practice.

t: Alcatraz versus dabelsti knihovnici (Alcatraz Versus the Evil Librarians)
why: A comic middle-grade fantasy narrated by its own hero, who interrupts himself, taunts the reader and cheerfully admits he is not to be trusted. Chapter one is one legible situation, not a fan-out: a stranger at the door claiming to be his grandfather, a stolen bag of sand, and a Librarian pointing a gun at him in the kitchen, so the failure that scored 30 three times over does not apply. The voice is the asset and it is well made, which is what holds the number in the 60s rather than lower. What the book does not do is leave an idea behind: the premise is a running gag about libraries hiding the truth, and Kirkus finds the joke tiresome by repetition with the similes stopping the narrative flow. That is precisely what stalled Narnia at 67, marked down for lacking higher things to think about, and Ranger's Apprentice at 74, easy to read but not much to think about. Comic invention can reach much higher - Hitchhiker's 83 - but that book has a real premise under the jokes. A thirteen-year-old lead is a further small pushback of the kind that cost Ender's Game points on re-reading. Leaned on the narrator rather than on the invented magic, which is played for silliness and is never asked to carry weight.

t: Alcatraz versus legie Zakladatelovych kosti (The Scrivener's Bones)
why: The engine is the same self-mocking first-person voice, and it is a real asset: one boy telling his own story, one situation at a time, no fan-out to be confused by. But this is a sequel, and sequels are not safe bets in this log - Hitchhiker's fell from 83 to 70, the steepest series decline recorded, and even Collins dropped from 89 to 83 when a sequel repeated a set piece for its own sake. The book widens the invented furniture rather than the thinking: a hidden city the family comes from, a library that takes your soul in exchange for a book, a part-metal antagonist. That is fun and it is consistent, but it is not an idea a reader carries away, and this reader's most common reason for a competent book to stall in the 60s is exactly that: Narnia 67 lacked higher things to think about, Ranger's Apprentice 74 was easy to read with little to think about. The metafictional joke also has to work a second time on a reader who has already met it, and the reported cost of that joke is broken momentum. A thirteen-year-old lead is a small further pushback. Leaned on the narrator, deliberately not on the worldbuilding, which is comic by design and never asked to hold up under thought.

RETRACTED AND RESET 2026-08-28, third pass. This line was raised earlier today on the argument that Valka stareho muze 87 proved sustained non-crude sexual content is cheap. The reader then corrected the premise: VSM's volume 'is not that big, it's mostly one chapter', so it proved nothing of the kind and that raise is withdrawn. What survives is the independent Witcher correction, worth about two points here. One premise stated precisely - a pump that trades matter with a neighbouring universe, giving everyone free energy while making the Sun certain to explode - and the entire book is that premise's consequences, including the political one, that nobody who benefits wants the calculation to be right. Project Hail Mary at 92 scores on exactly this. The middle section supplies three beings who each want different things: one resists her role, one wants a child, one trusts the authorities, and Golden Son at 92 is credited for precisely that. Deducted because three sections carry three separate casts and no single figure runs through the whole book; The Silmarillion at 80 shows that structure is survivable but not free. RAISED to this range earlier on 2026-08-28 from [68, 78], which had priced the alien union as a heavy volume deduction, and the comparator behind that deduction has since been withdrawn as well. Ruled 2026-08-28: The Witcher 53 is a CONFOUNDED row and cannot be cited as a sexual-axis floor - the reader named two independent causes, 'both magic (witches) and the sex was through out the series', and the magic is the occult filter, the most severe objection in the log. The clean crudeness anchor is Ready Player One 55 - 'it was the kind of sex that reduced it that much', the kind and not the amount - with Artemis 69 confirming crudeness costs even in small doses. VOLUME IS UNANCHORED and must not be priced as cheap: Red Rising 95 and Valka stareho muze 87 are BOTH low volume on the reader's own account ('mostly one chapter of a book'), so neither shows what sustained non-crude content costs, and the log's only high-volume row is the confounded one. Note also that VSM's single chapter was still enough to become his one named complaint, so light volume is not free. This book is the Valka stareho muze corner exactly - sustained but tender, crudeness absent, inside an SF novel whose premise is what carries it. Held at [72, 82] rather than raised again because the missing throughline, not the sexual axis, is now what caps it. Leaned on the idea and the worked-out mechanism, not on a protagonist, because there is no continuous one.

t: Anna na krku a jine povidky (Anna na krku a jine povidky)
why: The positive case is as strong as the form allows: this is a writer whose entire method is page time on what a person wants and why, with the incident cut to almost nothing - a provincial girl marries an old official for money and discovers what it makes of her - and that is exactly the axis that puts Red Rising 95, Mockingjay 91 and Speaker for the Dead 90 at the top of this log, delivered in clean prose of the kind that helped Ender's Game 87. Also in its favour: each story opens on one concrete situation, which is the opposite of the failure that ended The Gunslinger 30. What holds it under the line is the shape of this particular object. It is a career-spanning editor's selection of roughly forty-seven pieces across 399 pages, mixing early comic sketches with the mature work, so there is no one to follow and nothing accumulates - the complaint that put Unfinished Tales 69 at the bottom of the Tolkien range. And this author's declared position is to pose the question and refuse the answer, so what a reader carries away is a diagnosis of a life rather than an idea he can restate, which is the usual reason a good book stops in the 60s. I leaned on motives, not on ideas, for that reason.

Short stories, so the character and emotion rules are suspended - but the profile is explicit that the suspension removes penalties and never adds points, and there is nothing here to add them back. The positive case is the talk: ordinary men on the Prague periphery whose whole substance is what they want and how they narrate it, which is the axis behind Red Rising 95. Against that, the register is death sitting inside the banal - the title story opens on a girl's body found hanged in a suburban snack-bar arcade and then simply carries on with the afternoon - and sustained bleakness is a recorded discount: 1984 60 was too depressing, though Animal Farm 78 shows bleakness costs little when it leaves an idea behind. That is where the doubt sits. An editor's selection reshuffled across printings has no single premise to work out, so I would put ideas under risks, which is why I leaned on the short-form suspension and on motives instead.
